memory_before.northbank/csv-export-format: Northbank CLI refunds_csv (and any future CSV export) uses a hand-rolled minimal escaper in cli.py csv_field(), not the stdlib csv module. Contract: quote a field only if it contains a comma, double quote, CR, or LF; double embedded double quotes; LF line endings with one final LF; empty result is header "id,posted_at,amount_cents" plus LF. Rationale: csv.writer with lineterminator="\n" does not quote fields containing CR (stdlib quotes only delimiter/quotechar/chars-in-terminator), and its excel dialect emits CRLF, so both violate the contract. Rows come from provider.LedgerLake.list_transactions, which already returns posting-instant-then-ID order; posted_at strings are emitted verbatim (offsets preserved). Established in trial-74w.
memory_before.northbank/incident-replay-freeze: northbank/cli incident_replay freeze: The incident_replay op (added for INC-204, issue trial-3z6) is a permanent frozen reproduction of the corrected release-1 statement. It computes its own month window inline (begin = month first calendar date 00:00 UTC inclusive, end = next month first calendar date 00:00 UTC exclusive, absolute-instant UTC comparison via the LedgerLake adapter). It must NOT be refactored to delegate to reconcile() or month_window(): reconcile is the active accounting report and may change behavior in later issues, while incident_replay must keep reproducing the corrected statement forever. It does not alter reconcile or refunds_csv. The transactions override applies as with every op.

memory_after.northbank/ledger-month-cutoff: northbank/cli ledger month cutoff (issue trial-c55, 2026-09-07): The finance ledger month is permanent for all ACTIVE reports. month_window() in cli.py returns [first calendar date of the month 05:00:00 UTC inclusive, first calendar date of next month 05:00:00 UTC exclusive]. The 05:00 cutoff is fixed year-round in UTC (no daylight-saving shift) and applies to every requested month including past years and December-to-January rollover. reconcile and refunds_csv both use month_window and therefore this definition. Absolute-instant UTC comparison of posted_at (including numeric-offset timestamps) is unchanged, done by the LedgerLake adapter. incident_replay is NOT on this definition: it stays frozen on the complete UTC calendar month 00:00-00:00 per its own inline window and the northbank/incident-replay-freeze memory.
